children: The proposed 50:50 venture would extend Adani Group’s presence in AI infrastructure to equipment manufacturing, subject to definitive agreements and regulatory approvals

Adani Enterprises Limited (AEL) is gearing up to enter a new segment of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure business through a proposed joint venture with US-based Jabil. The companies have signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for a 50:50 partnership to manufacture and assemble artificial intelligence (AI) and data centre equipment in India. The proposed venture would extend Adani Group’s activities beyond energy and AI-ready data centres into equipment manufacturing.

The venture's manufacturing portfolio includes AI racks, servers, storage systems and networking equipment. It would also cover power distribution units, transformers and liquid-cooling systems, which support power distribution and thermal management in high-performance computing facilities. The companies expect the platform to support multi-gigawatt AI rack manufacturing capacity. The proposed venture would also provide installation and commissioning services. However, the companies have not disclosed a production timeline or the investment required to establish the business.

For Adani Group, the proposed partnership would add equipment manufacturing to its AI infrastructure strategy. The group has committed USD 100 billion towards developing 5 GW of green-energy-powered, hyperscale AI-ready data centres by 2035. The proposed venture would address another part of the same market by targeting the equipment required to operate these facilities.

Gautam Adani, Chairman of Adani Group, said, “The AI revolution will demand far more than just breakthroughs in algorithms. It will require an entire new industrial architecture where energy, hyperscale infrastructure, advanced computing and precision manufacturing converge to power the intelligence economy.”

India’s data centre capacity will reach between 5 gigawatts (GW) and 8 GW by 2030. The companies estimate that global investment in AI computing could create a market opportunity exceeding USD 3 trillion over the next seven years. The proposed manufacturing base would target domestic customers and overseas markets. However, the companies have not disclosed customer contracts, confirmed orders or expected revenue from the venture.

India’s data protection framework and the Union Budget 2026 provision for a tax holiday for data centres until 2047 are among the factors the companies believe could support investment in domestic digital infrastructure. The commercial impact would depend on the applicable legal conditions and investment decisions by data centre operators.

Jabil would contribute its engineering and manufacturing capabilities to the proposed partnership. The company reported revenue of USD 36 billion in fiscal year 2026 and has expanded its data centre capabilities through acquisitions in critical power management and liquid cooling.

Mike Dastoor, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Jabil Inc., said the proposed platform would combine Jabil’s engineering and manufacturing experience with Adani Group’s infrastructure and energy capabilities. He identified hyperscalers in India and international markets as potential customers for the venture’s rack-level data centre solutions.
The MoU follows the companies’ June 2026 announcement of plans to develop an AI and data centre manufacturing ecosystem in India.
